sentences.text: The brief facts giving rise to this appeal are that on 17 th April, 2011, the claimant-appellant, then aged 10 years, accompanied his mother to the market.

While crossing the road on NH-17/B near the BITS Pilani Campus, Zuari Nagar, Margoa, the offending vehicle, bearing registration number GA- 03/C-1944, dashed into the claimant-appellant in a rash and negligent manner.
Consequently, he sustained grievous injuries.
He initially took treatment at Goa Medical College, Bambolim.
Later, he was shifted to Dr. Oswal Hospital, Muddebihal.

He received further treatment at Kerodi Hospital,
Bagalkot and also at Dhanush Hospital, Bagalkot.
On account of injuries suffered, the appellant sustained permanent disability.

4. In connection with this incident, a case at Verna PS Crime No.50/11 was registered against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 337 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

5. An application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act for compensation before the Tribunal,
seeking compensation to the tune of Rs.35,50,000/- along with interest @ 18% was instituted on behalf of the claimant-appellant.

The Tribunal, vide its order, awarded an amount of Rs.11,57,500/-
to the claimant-appellant, along with interest @ 9%.

The Tribunal has awarded a lump sum amount Kumar Shivappa vs Filomina Dsuoza on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22213309/
1 of Rs.5,00,000/- for loss of earning capacity due to permanent disability determined to the extent of 90%.
6. Being aggrieved with the amount of compensation awarded, the claimant-appellant filed an appeal before the High Court for enhancement of the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

7. The High Court, vide the impugned order, enhanced the compensation by an amount of Rs.27,17,900/-, consequently, the total compensation arrived at was Rs.38,75,400/- along with interest @ 6% per annum.

The Court assessed the notional income as Rs.4,846/- per month by taking into account the decision rendered by this court in Kajal v. Jagdish Chand & Ors.1; and in Master Ayush v. the Branch Manager, Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. & Anr.2, wherein the notional income of the minor was assessed on the basis of minimum wages payable to the skilled workman.

entities.text: Master Ayush v. the Branch Manager, Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. & Anr.2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Yet dissatisfied, the claimant-appellant is now before us.

The significant points of the challenge taken are that the compensation awarded under the head of future treatment and attendant charges is on the lower side, as he is suffering from paraplegia, wherein he needs 24x7 assistance.

On the other hand, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Insurance company submitted that the High Court wrongly took the monthly income of the minor at Rs.4,846/-, whereas it should be Rs.4,014/- per month as per the minimum wage of the skilled worker at the time of the accident.
10. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties.
11. We are unable to agree with the view taken by the High Court in assessing the notional income of the claimant- appellant.

We advert to the principle laid down in Master Ayush (supra) and Baby Sakshi Greola v. Manzoor Ahmad Simon & Anr.3, wherein it was stated that in motor vehicle accident claims, the income of the minor is taken, at least, as per the minimum wages payable to a skilled workman in the concerned State.

entities.text: Baby Sakshi Greola v. Manzoor Ahmad Simon & Anr.3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the present case, in view of the above exposition of law,
the monthly income of the skilled worker would be at Rs.4,014/-, as per the Notification annexed as Annexure R/2-1 to Counter Affidavit, as per the Minimum Wage Schedule for the period from 1st April, 2011 to 31st March, 2012.
However, since the Tribunal took the income to be Rs.4,846/-, we are not inclined, in the attending facts and circumstances, to reduce the same.
Furthermore, we agree with the contention of the claimant-appellant on the amounts under the heads of future treatment and attendant charges.
